clue.text: Lines getting mimic in a flap

indicators.note: the mimic word is placed in the middle of the two letters standing for lines

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for line, so two of them (lines) give LL
to ape someone is to mimic them

explanation.surface: Someone flustered because their lines are being mimicked by a copycat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a flap' reads as an idiom for panic, but 'in' is the container signal and 'flap' alone is the definition, with 'a' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The folded-back flap on the front of a jacket is called by this tailoring term.

clue.text: Mounted colonel kept barking about singular marching style

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word is read bottom to top
the scrambled letters go around the letter for singular
barking means mad, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A colonel on horseback barking orders about a parade-ground march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' turns KEPT into KTEP, which goes around S.
explanation.definitionFit: Marching in lockstep means moving in close, exact unison, one behind another.

clue.text: See inside cut with plaster on

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other

parts.note: pared means cut or trimmed
to get something is to see or understand it

explanation.surface: Notice the trimmed interior wall with its fresh plaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Pargeting is ornamental plasterwork on walls, so a pargeted surface has plaster on it.

clue.text: I've split the atom! — smashed to make this novel form

indicators.note: smashed means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scientist's triumphant cry about splitting the atom.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram fodder is the whole exclamation; 'to make this' and 'form' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a P. G. Wodehouse comic novel from 1923.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about New York team that's versatile

indicators.note: the enthusiasm word goes around the other two pieces like a fence

parts.note: mad about something means very keen on it
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: A fan keen on a New York sports team that can do anything.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with many sides to their talent is versatile; the hyphenated phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Cover reaching calves in the south of France

definitions.meaning: a skirt or coat of mid-calf length
the French name for the southern region of France

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a mid-calf garment length and is also the French term for southern France.

clue.text: British channels worked up controversies when involving English

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ran means worked, as a machine runs

indicators.note: the English letter is included within the other pieces

parts.note: rows are arguments or controversies
as can mean when

explanation.surface: British TV channels stirred up arguments involving the English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Channels' suggests television, but these are sea channels.
explanation.definitionFit: The English Channel and the Strait of Dover were historically called by this name.

clue.text: Governed economy arbitrarily sets cap at a limit

indicators.note: arbitrarily means without order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A government arbitrarily capping something at a limit.
explanation.definitionFit: An economy where the government owns and directs business is a form of state-run capitalism.

clue.text: Perhaps spoil an eternity after the very first year?

indicators.note: the eternity piece comes after the year piece

parts.note: the year dot means the very beginning of time
an eon is an age, an eternity

explanation.surface: An eternity has passed since the very first year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Since the year dot' is a British idiom for since time began.
explanation.definitionFit: To spoil a child is one way to adore and indulge them excessively, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Respectable parents disowning son?

indicators.note: disowning means rejecting, so the letter for son is removed

parts.note: descent means parentage or ancestry

explanation.surface: Respectable parents cutting off their son.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent person is respectable, proper and honest.

clue.text: Royal dog with its owner shunning good ingredient of coronation chicken?

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so the letter for good is left out of the dog

parts.note: the corgi is famously the breed kept by the British royal family
with can mean and, joining two things
the corgi's owner was the Queen, ER (Elizabeth Regina)

explanation.surface: A royal corgi and the Queen together, with a nod to the dish made for her coronation.
explanation.walkthrough: Coronation chicken is a cold curried chicken dish created for Elizabeth II's coronation in 1953; ER is the crossword convention for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: This herb is one of the spices used in the curry dressing for coronation chicken, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Eccentric once favouring Labour?

definitions.meaning: an archaic adjective meaning grotesque or bizarre
read as two parts, against C, i.e. opposed to the Conservatives, Labour's main rival

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned oddball who used to support the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into ANTI plus C, the abbreviation for Conservative, so favouring Labour is jokily equated with opposing the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: As an old adjective the word meant grotesque or fantastic, close to eccentric in older English.

clue.text: Middle East money I'll get out of Arab leader, plus contents of well

indicators.note: the letter must leave the Arab leader, so it is removed from that word

parts.note: a sheik is an Arab chief
read as I will, so the letter I is the one that will get out

indicators.note: the inner letters of the word well, with its outer letters dropped

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to escape a sheikh and take water from a well for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the currency of Israel, a country in the Middle East.

clue.text: Disappointment is something funny, almost peculiar

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

parts.note: a comedy is something funny
peculiar in its old sense means one's own, particular to oneself

explanation.surface: A let-down that is half joke and half oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedown is a decline in status or an anticlimax, a synonym of disappointment.

clue.text: Shampoos are such defences

definitions.meaning: read as two words, shampoos are meant for hair

explanation.surface: Hair products marketed as protection.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into FOR TRESSES: shampoos are for tresses, a poetic word for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortified strongholds are defences, built to resist attack.

clue.text: Judge overruling Liberal in ballot constituency provides a get-out when going down

indicators.note: the judge letter overrules, taking the place of, the letter for Liberal

parts.note: a ballot is an election
a seat is a parliamentary constituency

explanation.surface: Election talk: a judge overrules a Liberal over a constituency vote.
explanation.walkthrough: The political surface hides an aircraft device; 'provides' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot's escape mechanism fires them out of a plane that is crashing.

clue.text: A French knight was a rival not exciting jealousy

parts.note: une is the French feminine word for a
N is the chess notation for knight
vied means competed, was a rival

explanation.surface: A French knight competed but nobody envied him.
explanation.definitionFit: Something nobody is jealous of is not envied by anyone.

clue.text: US military leaders confine with electronic device attached

parts.note: to pen is to confine
an electronic tag is a monitoring device
on means attached, as in something being on

explanation.surface: Confining someone with an electronic tag fitted to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pentagon is the US Defense Department headquarters, used to mean the top military leadership.

clue.text: Went snap and was beaten at cards by nobody?

parts.note: lost means was beaten
patience is a card game played alone, so whoever wins, nobody else is beating you

explanation.surface: Someone lost their temper after being beaten at cards by a nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snap' looks like the card game, but 'went snap' means lost one's temper; patience is the solitaire game for one player.
explanation.definitionFit: To snap is to lose one's temper suddenly, an idiom for running out of composure.

clue.text: Look forward to taking head off a Books Fi prophet

clue.text: Take on breadth of character with a joke and energy

parts.note: an en is a printer's measure, the width of a letter N
a gag is a joke
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Hiring someone of broad character with humour and drive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' means a printed letter, not a person; 'with a' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: To engage staff is to take them on, hire them.

clue.text: They stay in touch, communicating with flags

definitions.text: They stay in touch, communicating with flags

parts.words: They stay in touch, communicating with flags
parts.note: reads as people keeping in contact by semaphore, but describes the officials who run along the touchline in football or rugby waving flags

explanation.surface: Signallers keeping contact with each other by flag.
explanation.walkthrough: In football and rugby, touch is the area beyond the side lines; the assistant officials patrol it and signal with flags.
explanation.definitionFit: These match officials keep to the touchline and raise flags to signal decisions.

clue.text: Locks obstruct goal

parts.note: to bar is to obstruct
the net is the goal in football

explanation.surface: Locks that block access to a target.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Locks' suggests fastenings but means hair; the answer is Cockney rhyming slang, Barnet Fair for hair.
explanation.definitionFit: In British rhyming slang this word means hair, and locks are hair too.

clue.text: What's regularly expressed in bedrooms?

indicators.note: every other letter of bedrooms is taken

explanation.surface: Wondering what is often voiced in bedrooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love and desire, or erotic love itself, is fittingly expressed in bedrooms.

clue.text: Healthy retreat greeting old Turkish soldier …

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A health resort welcoming a veteran Ottoman trooper.
explanation.definitionFit: Spahis were cavalrymen in the old Ottoman Turkish army.

clue.text: … making raids — thus Resistance coordinate end of fighting

parts.note: so means thus
R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to tie in is to coordinate or link up

indicators.note: the final letter of the word fighting

explanation.surface: The Resistance coordinating its operations as the fighting ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues from the previous one via the ellipsis; the Resistance surface fits the wartime idea of sorties.
explanation.definitionFit: A sortie is a raid out from a defended position, and this is its verb form.

clue.text: Stones producing intro for track they mass distributed

indicators.note: distributed means spread out, so the letters are rearranged
the opening letter of the word track

explanation.surface: Introducing a track that a crowd spreads out over.
explanation.definitionFit: These purple quartz gems are precious stones.

clue.text: Not any stupid, backward or perhaps silly man

indicators.note: both pieces are written backwards as one run

parts.note: no means not any
dim means stupid

explanation.surface: Insulting a man as dim and backward, or simply silly.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, mid-on is a fielding position; silly mid-on is a closer variant, so a mid-on fielder is perhaps silly.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket fielder in this position can be the silly version, standing close to the batsman.
